claim: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality in men and women, surpassing combined deaths from colon, prostate and breast cancer.
source: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality in men and women, surpassing combined deaths from colon, prostate and breast cancer (https://www.cancer.org/, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to cancer.org, 2019

claim: Approximately 40% of non-small cell carcinoma (NSCLC) is of the adenocarcinoma subtype.
source: Approximately 40% of non-small cell carcinoma (NSCLC) is of the adenocarcinoma subtype.
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about NSCLC classification

claim: Genomic alterations of KRAS and TP53 mutations are the most frequent events within the adenocarcinoma subtype.
source: Genomic alterations of KRAS and TP53 mutations are the most frequent events within this tumor subtype (Cancer Genome Atlas Research, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cancer Genome Atlas Research, 2014

claim: Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells are the predominant cell of origin of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD).
source: Considerable evidence indicates that alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells are the predominant cell of origin of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) (Desai et al., 2014; Mainardi et al., 2014; Sutherland et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations: Desai et al., 2014; Mainardi et al., 2014; Sutherland et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2012

claim: Sustained tumor growth is maintained, in some instances, by a subset of plastic, stem-like cells, referred to as tumor-propagating cells (TPCs).
source: Sustained tumor growth is maintained, in some instances, by a subset of plastic, stem-like cells, referred to as tumor-propagating cells (TPCs) (Batlle and Clevers, 2017; Beck and Blanpain, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Batlle and Clevers, 2017; Beck and Blanpain, 2013

claim: TPCs are less sensitive to therapeutic intervention and functionally contribute to tumor regrowth following treatment responses.
source: This rare cell subset is less sensitive to therapeutic intervention, and functionally contributes to tumor regrowth following treatment responses (Beck and Blanpain, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Beck and Blanpain, 2013

claim: TPCs in LUAD have been previously characterized and were shown to be required for KrasG12D tumor self-renewal.
source: TPCs in LUAD have been previously characterized and were shown to be required for KrasG12D tumor self-renewal (Zheng et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zheng et al., 2013

claim: A TPC gene signature correlates with poor prognosis in non-small cell LUAD patients.
source: Moreover, a TPC gene signature correlates with poor prognosis in non-small cell LUAD patients (Zheng et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zheng et al., 2013

claim: Wnt signaling is critical in the distal airway to maintain AT2 cell fate and function in the alveolar compartment.
source: Wnt signaling is critical in the distal airway to maintain AT2 cell fate and function in the alveolar compartment.
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about Wnt signaling in lung biology

claim: A subset of AT2 cells serve as adult tissue stem cells, replenishing themselves, as well as alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells.
source: A subset of AT2 cells serve as adult tissue stem cells, replenishing themselves, as well as alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells, which are both required to maintain proper alveolar function.
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about AT2 cell function

claim: Deletion of β-catenin in AT2 cells leads to AT1 cell fate differentiation.
source: Deletion of β-catenin in AT2 cells leads to AT1 cell fate differentiation, demonstrating that β-catenin-mediated Wnt signaling is required for AT2 cell identity (Frank et al., 2016; Nabhan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Frank et al., 2016; Nabhan et al., 2018

claim: β-catenin-mediated Wnt signaling is required for AT2 cell identity.
source: Deletion of β-catenin in AT2 cells leads to AT1 cell fate differentiation, demonstrating that β-catenin-mediated Wnt signaling is required for AT2 cell identity (Frank et al., 2016; Nabhan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Frank et al., 2016; Nabhan et al., 2018

claim: Forced expression of a stabilized form of β-catenin engenders aberrant cell fate in mouse lung.
source: Along the same lines, genetic models have also shown the forced expression of a stabilized form of β-catenin engenders aberrant cell fate in mouse lung (Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011

claim: Disruption of Wnt signaling equilibrium can have major consequences in some disease pathologies, including lung cancer.
source: Furthermore, disruption of Wnt signaling equilibrium can have major consequences in some disease pathologies, including lung cancer (Nabhan et al., 2018; Tammela et al., 2017; Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nabhan et al., 2018; Tammela et al., 2017; Zacharias et al., 2018

claim: Expression of the EHMT2 lysine methyltransferase (G9a) is a poor prognostic factor in LUAD.
source: Recent work identified expression of the EHMT2 lysine methyltransferase (G9a) as a poor prognostic factor in LUAD (Chen et al., 2010; Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chen et al., 2010; Huang et al., 2017

claim: EHMT2 activity has been implicated in the regulation of cell identity during development primarily through its epigenetic histone methyltransferase activity.
source: Interestingly, EHMT2 activity has been implicated in the regulation of cell identity during development primarily through its epigenetic histone methyltransferase activity (Chen et al., 2012; Epsztejn-Litman et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chen et al., 2012; Epsztejn-Litman et al., 2008

claim: EHMT2 protein expression is robustly increased in the TPC population compared to non-TPC.
source: Using two distinct detection methods we observed a consistent and robust increase in EHMT2 protein expression (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Western blot and flow cytometry (Figure 1A-C)

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT2 using UNC0642 resulted in a dose-dependent decrease of primary ex vivo KP-derived tumorsphere formation.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT2, using UNC0642 (Liu et al., 2013), resulted in a dose-dependent decrease of primary ex vivo KP-derived tumorsphere formation (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and citation to Liu et al., 2013 for the inhibitor

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT2 in established tumorspheres led to a marked reduction in both histone H3 lysine 9 di- and tri-methylation marks (H3K9me2/3).
source: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT2 in established tumorspheres led to a marked reduction in both histone H3 lysine 9 di- and tri-methylation marks (H3K9me2/3), consistent with potent EHMT2 inhibition (Collins and Cheng, 2010; Epsztejn-Litman et al., 2008; Shinkai and Tachibana, 2011; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citations to Collins and Cheng, 2010; Epsztejn-Litman et al., 2008; Shinkai and Tachibana, 2011

claim: Both UNC0642 treatment and shRNA-mediated depletion of Ehmt2 impaired secondary sphere formation.
source: Both UNC0642 treatment or short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated depletion of Ehmt2 similarly impaired secondary sphere formation (Figure 1F–I), albeit only shEHMT2.2 reached statistical significance, establishing a requirement for EHMT2 activity in TPC self-renewal.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F-I

claim: EHMT2 activity is required for TPC self-renewal.
source: Both UNC0642 treatment or short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated depletion of Ehmt2 similarly impaired secondary sphere formation (Figure 1F–I), albeit only shEHMT2.2 reached statistical significance, establishing a requirement for EHMT2 activity in TPC self-renewal.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing impaired sphere formation upon EHMT2 inhibition/depletion (Figure 1F-I)

claim: Sorted shEhmt2-expressing cells from primary recipients showed a significant decrease in both ex vivo tumorspheres and in vivo secondary tumor formation.
source: Sorted shEhmt2-expressing cells from primary recipients showed a significant decrease in both ex vivo tumorspheres and in vivo secondary tumor formation, establishing a role for EHMT2 in maintaining TPC stemness (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-D

claim: EHMT2 plays a role in maintaining TPC stemness.
source: Sorted shEhmt2-expressing cells from primary recipients showed a significant decrease in both ex vivo tumorspheres and in vivo secondary tumor formation, establishing a role for EHMT2 in maintaining TPC stemness (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing decreased tumorsphere and tumor formation with EHMT2 depletion (Figure 2A-D)

claim: Continuous monitoring of secondary transplants in vivo revealed a substantial growth impairment in shEhmt2-expressing tumors, which translated to a significant increase in overall survival.
source: Continuous monitoring of secondary transplants in vivo revealed a substantial growth impairment in sh Ehmt2 -expressing tumors, which translated to a significant increase in overall survival (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E-F

claim: Mice harboring shEhmt2-expressing tumors eventually succumb to tumor outgrowth with re-expression of Ehmt2 transcript to a level equivalent to that of control tumors.
source: Mice harboring shEhmt2-expressing tumors eventually succumb to tumor outgrowth; however, analysis of terminal tumors revealed re-expression of Ehmt2 transcript to a level equivalent to that of control tumors (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B

claim: Ehmt2 expression is required for TPC-tumor growth.
source: This data demonstrates that Ehmt2 expression is required for TPC-tumor growth.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that tumors with Ehmt2 knockdown show impaired growth and that terminal tumors re-express Ehmt2

claim: EHMT2 activity in TPCs functions to maintain the self-renewal capacity of KP tumors.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that EHMT2 activity in TPCs functions to maintain the self-renewal capacity of KP tumors.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing impaired tumor growth and self-renewal upon EHMT2 inhibition/depletion

claim: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in significant reductions in BrdU-labeled cells (fivefold).
source: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in significant reductions in BrdU-labeled cells (fivefold) and expression of cleaved caspase-3 (>10 fold) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D

claim: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in significant increase in expression of cleaved caspase-3 (>10 fold).
source: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in significant reductions in BrdU-labeled cells (fivefold) and expression of cleaved caspase-3 (>10 fold) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D

claim: The AT2 gene signature was significantly increased following EHMT2 inhibition, in contrast to other cell lineages.
source: The AT2 gene signature was significantly increased following EHMT2 inhibition, in contrast to other cell lineages (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data and enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3A

claim: Protein expression of surfactant protein C (SPC), a canonical AT2 marker, was significantly upregulated in EHMT2-inhibited tumorspheres.
source: Protein expression of surfactant protein C (SPC), a canonical AT2 marker was also significantly upregulated in EHMT2 -inhibited tumorspheres, likely due to differentiated progenitors (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: EHMT2 inhibition showed an increase in CD74, an additional cell surface marker characterizing AT2 cells, with an increase of the double-positive population (1.8-fold).
source: Concomitant with an increase in SPC+, we observed an increase in CD74, an additional cell surface marker characterizing AT2 cells (Lee et al., 2013), showing an increase of the double-positive population (1.8-fold) (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B-C and citation to Lee et al., 2013

claim: There was a significant increase in the transcript levels of multiple surfactants in both EHMT2-inhibited and EHMT2-depleted (shEhmt2) tumorspheres.
source: Moreover, we observed a significant increase in the transcript levels of multiple surfactants in both EHMT2-inhibited and EHMT2-depleted (shEhmt2) tumorspheres (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.B), indicating increased/enhanced AT2-like cell fate features when EHMT2 activity is impaired.
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B

claim: EHMT2 inhibition triggers an enhanced/reinforced AT2-like cell state in KP-derived tumorspheres.
source: Together these results demonstrate that EHMT2 inhibition triggers an enhanced/reinforced AT2-like cell state in KP-derived tumorspheres.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing increased AT2 markers and morphological features upon EHMT2 inhibition

claim: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of EHMT2-inhibited tumorspheres revealed a significant increase in lamellar bodies.
source: Furthermore, evidence supporting cell fate transition was observed when transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of EHMT2-inhibited tumorspheres revealed a significant increase in lamellar bodies (Balis and Conen, 1964), which are distinct specialized structures responsible for the storage and release of surfactants and serve as a morphometric readout for AT2 cells (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3D-E and citation to Balis and Conen, 1964

claim: Lamellar bodies are distinct specialized structures responsible for the storage and release of surfactants and serve as a morphometric readout for AT2 cells.
source: Furthermore, evidence supporting cell fate transition was observed when transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of EHMT2-inhibited tumorspheres revealed a significant increase in lamellar bodies (Balis and Conen, 1964), which are distinct specialized structures responsible for the storage and release of surfactants and serve as a morphometric readout for AT2 cells (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about lamellar body function and citation to Balis and Conen, 1964

claim: EHMT2 inhibition in primary tumorspheres caused a reduction in TPCs.
source: EHMT2 inhibition in primary tumorspheres caused a reduction in TPCs, (Figure 3—figure supplement 5), consistent with their reduced stemness.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5

claim: EHMT2-inhibited TPCs displayed a statistically significant increase (fourfold) in the AT2 surface markers, SPC and CD74, compared to matched controls.
source: Notably, EHMT2-inhibited TPCs displayed a statistically significant increase (fourfold) in the AT2 surface markers, SPC and CD74, compared to matched controls (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F-G

claim: Sftpc and Cd74 transcripts increased exclusively in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition.
source: Consistently, Sftpc and Cd74 transcripts increased exclusively in TPCs (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3H

claim: EHMT2 inhibition leads to an induced AT2-like cell state within the TPC subset, thereby reducing their regenerative capacity by a mechanism similar in features to differentiation.
source: Together, these data indicate that EHMT2 inhibition leads to an induced AT2-like cell state within the TPC subset, thereby reducing their regenerative capacity by a mechanism similar in features to differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing increased AT2 markers and reduced stemness in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition

claim: EHMT2 gene expression negatively correlates with the AT2 cell gene signature in human LUAD.
source: Consistent with our murine data, EHMT2 gene expression negatively correlates with the AT2 cell gene signature (Figure 3—figure supplement 6), supporting the concept that EHMT2 activity impairs differentiation.
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6

claim: EHMT2 activity represses an alveolar differentiation program in murine LUAD as a means to preserve stem-like properties that enable tumor self-renewal.
source: Taken together, the data indicate that EHMT2 activity represses an alveolar differentiation program in murine LUAD as a means to preserve stem-like properties that enable tumor self-renewal.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing that EHMT2 inhibition induces AT2 differentiation and impairs self-renewal

claim: Very limited changes in chromatin accessibility were observed in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition.
source: Surprisingly, very limited changes in chromatin accessibility were observed in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B), indicating that EHMT2 inhibition does not induce widespread chromatin remodeling: 11 promoter and 320 non-promoter sites became more accessible following EHMT2 inhibition, whereas 3 promoter and 54 non-promoter sites were less accessible (FDR <0.05, fold-change >1.5).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: EHMT2 inhibition does not induce widespread chromatin remodeling.
source: Surprisingly, very limited changes in chromatin accessibility were observed in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B), indicating that EHMT2 inhibition does not induce widespread chromatin remodeling: 11 promoter and 320 non-promoter sites became more accessible following EHMT2 inhibition, whereas 3 promoter and 54 non-promoter sites were less accessible (FDR <0.05, fold-change >1.5).
evidence: Inferred from ATAC-seq data showing limited chromatin accessibility changes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B)

claim: A subset of AT2 cells in normal lung act as tissue stem cells, and Wnt signaling is critical for the maintenance of their stem cell identity.
source: A subset of AT2 cells in normal lung act as tissue stem cells, and Wnt signaling is critical for the maintenance of their stem cell identity (Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018

claim: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in a statistically significant increase in Axin2 expression only within the TPC subset.
source: Consistent with this line of reasoning, EHMT2 inhibition resulted in a statistically significant increase in Axin2 expression only within the TPC subset (Figure 4A), implicating a functional link between EHMT2 activity and Wnt signaling.
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4A

claim: There is a functional link between EHMT2 activity and Wnt signaling.
source: Consistent with this line of reasoning, EHMT2 inhibition resulted in a statistically significant increase in Axin2 expression only within the TPC subset (Figure 4A), implicating a functional link between EHMT2 activity and Wnt signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that EHMT2 inhibition increases Axin2 expression (Figure 4A)

claim: Pharmacological activation of Wnt signaling using two doses of the GSK3β inhibitor CHIR99021 impaired TPC stemness as illustrated by reduced tumorsphere self-renewal.
source: Indeed, pharmacological activation of Wnt signaling using two doses of the GSK3β inhibitor CHIR99021 (Figure 4B and Figure 4C) impaired TPC stemness as illustrated by reduced tumorsphere self-renewal, consistent with EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 4B–F).
evidence: Supported by tumorsphere formation assay data shown in Figure 4B-C

claim: Wnt pathway activation with CHIR99021 led to transcriptional activation of AT2 marker genes at secondary passage.
source: Moreover, corresponding Wnt pathway activation and transcriptional activation of AT2 marker genes was observed at secondary passage (Figure 4E), with a concordant dose-dependent increase in SPC surface expression (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E-F

claim: The Tcf4 motif ranked eighth among 264 tested motifs for AT2 genes, while ranking much lower for other cell lineages.
source: We found that the Tcf4 motif ranked eighth among 264 tested motifs for AT2 genes, while ranking much lower for other cell lineages, supporting the concept that AT2 cell fate is directly linked to a Wnt-driven signaling process (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: AT2 cell fate is directly linked to a Wnt-driven signaling process.
source: We found that the Tcf4 motif ranked eighth among 264 tested motifs for AT2 genes, while ranking much lower for other cell lineages, supporting the concept that AT2 cell fate is directly linked to a Wnt-driven signaling process (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Inferred from motif enrichment analysis showing Tcf4 motif enrichment in AT2 genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2)

claim: 4 out of 7 Tcf4-containing AT2 genes are significantly induced in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition.
source: Moreover, 4 out of 7 Tcf4-containing AT2 genes are significantly induced in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), further supporting the concept that the EHMT2 -inhibitor phenotype is Wnt-mediated.
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3

claim: The EHMT2-inhibitor phenotype is Wnt-mediated.
source: Moreover, 4 out of 7 Tcf4-containing AT2 genes are significantly induced in TPCs upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), further supporting the concept that the EHMT2 -inhibitor phenotype is Wnt-mediated.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Tcf4-containing AT2 genes are induced upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 3)

claim: The Tcf4-containing AT2 genes that are induced upon EHMT2 inhibition display accessible chromatin configurations at their promoters irrespective of treatment.
source: Notably, the Tcf4-containing AT2 genes that are induced upon EHMT2 inhibition display accessible chromatin configurations at their promoters irrespective of treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), suggesting that these genes are poised to respond to Wnt-mediated signals and therefore would not require chromatin accessibility changes to enable gene expression (Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and citation to Zacharias et al., 2018

claim: Tcf4-containing AT2 genes are poised to respond to Wnt-mediated signals and therefore would not require chromatin accessibility changes to enable gene expression.
source: Notably, the Tcf4-containing AT2 genes that are induced upon EHMT2 inhibition display accessible chromatin configurations at their promoters irrespective of treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), suggesting that these genes are poised to respond to Wnt-mediated signals and therefore would not require chromatin accessibility changes to enable gene expression (Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: Inferred from ATAC-seq data showing accessible chromatin at these promoters regardless of treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 4) and citation to Zacharias et al., 2018

claim: RUVBL2 has been shown to antagonize β-catenin activity.
source: RUVBL2 has also been shown to antagonize β-catenin activity (Bauer et al., 2000; Mao and Houry, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bauer et al., 2000; Mao and Houry, 2017

claim: EHMT2-dependent methylation of the non-histone substrate RUVBL2 can repress HIF1α-mediated transcription.
source: Previous reports have shown that EHMT2 -dependent methylation of the non-histone substrate RUVBL2 (REPTIN, TIP48, and TIP49b) can repress HIF1α-mediated transcription (Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2010

claim: RUVBL2 interacts with β-catenin and HIF1-α proteins in hypoxic and normoxic conditions.
source: Immunoprecipitation of RUVBL2 showed its ability to interact with β-catenin and HIF1-α proteins in hypoxic and normoxic conditions (Figure 5A), consistent with previously reported results (Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A and citation to Lee et al., 2010

claim: The RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction was reduced exclusively in the EHMT2-inhibited context.
source: Reciprocally, immunoprecipitation of β-catenin showed an interaction with RUVBL2. However, the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction was reduced exclusively in the EHMT2 -inhibited context (Figure 5B), indicating that the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction requires EHMT2 activity, analogous to that of the RUVBL2-HIF-1α (Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B and citation to Lee et al., 2010

claim: The RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction requires EHMT2 activity.
source: Reciprocally, immunoprecipitation of β-catenin showed an interaction with RUVBL2. However, the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction was reduced exclusively in the EHMT2 -inhibited context (Figure 5B), indicating that the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction requires EHMT2 activity, analogous to that of the RUVBL2-HIF-1α (Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Inferred from co-immunoprecipitation data showing reduced interaction upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 5B) and citation to Lee et al., 2010

claim: Proximity ligation assay (PLA) confirmed the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction in TPCs and demonstrated a significant loss of signal in the presence of EHMT2 inhibitor.
source: Indeed, PLA confirmed the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction in TPCs and demonstrated a significant loss of signal in the presence of EHMT2 I, providing additional support for the requirement of EHMT2 activity to maintain the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Supported by PLA data shown in Figure 5C-D

claim: EHMT2 activity is required to maintain the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction.
source: Indeed, PLA confirmed the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction in TPCs and demonstrated a significant loss of signal in the presence of EHMT2 I, providing additional support for the requirement of EHMT2 activity to maintain the RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Inferred from PLA data showing loss of RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction signal upon EHMT2 inhibition (Figure 5C-D)

claim: EHMT2 inhibition showed loss of both EHMT2 and RUVBL2 proteins from the chromatin fraction, while equal amounts of β-catenin remain chromatin-bound.
source: While EHMT2 inhibition showed loss of both EHMT2 and RUVBL2 proteins from the chromatin fraction, equal amounts of β-catenin remain chromatin-bound (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 5E

claim: The sustained levels of chromatin-bound β-catenin following EHMT2 inhibition suggests a critical role for EHMT2-mediated RUVBL2 regulation that occurs at the chromatin.
source: The sustained levels of chromatin-bound β-catenin following EHMT2 inhibition, suggests a critical role for EHMT2 -mediated RUVBL2 regulation that occurs at the chromatin (Figure 5E).
evidence: Inferred from subcellular fractionation data showing β-catenin remains chromatin-bound while RUVBL2 is lost (Figure 5E)

claim: There was over 90% reduction in RUVBL2 promoter occupancy within Tcf4 elements of AT2 genes Slc34a2 and Etv5 upon EHMT2 inhibition.
source: We observed over 90% reduction in RUVBL2 promoter occupancy within Tcf4 elements of AT2 genes Slc34a2 and Etv5 (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5F-G

claim: EHMT2 directly controls Tcf4-containing AT2 gene expression through RUVBL2-mediated repression of β-catenin transcription.
source: Taken together these results indicate that EHMT2 directly controls Tcf4-containing AT2 gene expression through RUVBL2-mediated repression of β-catenin transcription.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing EHMT2 regulates RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction and RUVBL2 chromatin occupancy at AT2 gene promoters

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT2 in vivo for 6 days demonstrated a robust induction of Axin2 protein expression in primary distal alveolar cells.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT2 in vivo for 6 days demonstrated a robust induction of Axin2 protein expression in primary distal alveolar cells using flow cytometry (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: Inhibition of EHMT2 activity did not impair ex vivo alveosphere formation; however, the resulting spheres were significantly smaller relative to controls.
source: In contrast to KP tumorspheres, inhibition of EHMT2 activity did not impair ex vivo alveosphere formation; however, the resulting spheres were significantly smaller relative to controls (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by alveosphere formation assay data shown in Figure 6B

claim: EHMT2 inhibition significantly reduced the proportion of AT1 cells (SPC-PDPN+) from 67.2 to 24.4%.
source: By analyzing expression of surface markers indicative of these fates (Desai et al., 2014), we observed that EHMT2 inhibition significantly reduced the proportion of AT1 cells (SPC-PDPN+) from 67.2 to 24.4% (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and citation to Desai et al., 2014

claim: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in a marked increase in double positive cells (SPC+PDPN+) from 15 to 62%.
source: Interestingly, while the proportion of AT2 cells (SPC +PDPN-) remained unchanged, we observed a marked increase in double positive cells (SPC +PDPN + ) from 15 to 62%.
evidence: Inferred from flow cytometry data showing changes in cell populations

claim: EHMT2 is required for differentiation of the AT2 progenitor pool and for complete and proper AT1 differentiation.
source: Together these data indicate that EHMT2 is required for differentiation of the AT2 progenitor pool and for complete and proper AT1 differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations showing impaired AT1 differentiation and accumulation of intermediate cells upon EHMT2 inhibition

claim: EHMT2 inhibition resulted in enhanced Wnt signaling in primary AT2 cells, reflected by increased Axin2 expression, as well as Lgr4 and Lgr5.
source: Consistent with our previous results in TPCs, EHMT2 inhibition resulted in enhanced Wnt signaling, reflected by increased Axin2 expression, as well as Lgr4 and Lgr5, two prominent Wnt signaling pathway components (de Lau et al., 2011; Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6D and citation to de Lau et al., 2011

claim: The observed increase in Tcf4-containing AT2 marker gene expression supports increased Wnt-mediated activity in primary AT2 cells as in the TPC context.
source: The observed increase in Tcf4-containing AT2 marker gene expression supports increased Wnt-mediated activity in primary AT2 cells as in the TPC context (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6E

claim: EHMT2-mediated regulation of Wnt signaling and cell fate is observable in untransformed, primary AT2 cells.
source: These data demonstrate that EHMT2-mediated regulation of Wnt signaling and cell fate is also observable in untransformed, primary AT2 cells.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations showing similar Wnt signaling and cell fate effects in primary AT2 cells as in TPCs

claim: EHMT2 loss in the alveolar compartment showed a significant 2.5-fold increase in double positive (SPC+PDPN+) cells, in just 4 days following hyperoxic injury.
source: EHMT2 loss in the alveolar compartment showed a significant 2.5-fold increase in double positive (SPC + PDPN + ) cells, in just 4 days following injury consistent with our ex vivo alveosphere findings (Figure 6—figure supplement 6F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 6F

claim: EHMT2 functions as a cell intrinsic mechanism to directly control cell fate decisions in the context of primary, untransformed AT2 cells.
source: All together these data demonstrate that EHMT2 functions as a cell intrinsic mechanism to directly control cell fate decisions in the context of primary, untransformed AT2 cells.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations in primary AT2 cells showing EHMT2 regulates Wnt signaling and cell fate

claim: KPE mice showed a striking reduction in tumor formation and significant decrease in tumor burden in comparison to KP mice, which translated to a significant increase in overall survival.
source: KPE mice showed a striking reduction in tumor formation and significant decrease in tumor burden in comparison to KP mice, which translated to a significant increase in overall survival (Figure 6—figure supplement 7A,B).
evidence: Supported by tumor monitoring and survival data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 7A,B

claim: The observed increase in overall survival in both KPE and KE mice was independent of p53 status.
source: Of note, the observed increase in overall survival in both KPE and KE mice was independent of p53 status.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of survival data between KPE and KE mice

claim: EHMT2 is crucial for Kras-mediated tumor initiation.
source: These results demonstrate that EHMT2 is crucial for Kras-mediated tumor initiation and are consistent with the requirement of EHMT2 to enable AT2 and TPC regenerative capacity and cell fate.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations showing reduced tumor formation in KPE and KE mice

claim: EHMT2 methyltransferase regulates Wnt signaling in the lung by controlling the transcriptional activity of chromatin-bound β-catenin, through a non-histone substrate in mouse lung.
source: Here, we discover that EHMT2 methyltransferase regulates Wnt signaling in the lung by controlling the transcriptional activity of chromatin-bound β-catenin, through a non-histone substrate in mouse lung.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing EHMT2 regulates RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction and Wnt signaling

claim: Inhibition of EHMT2 induces transcriptional, morphologic, and molecular changes consistent with alveolar type 2 (AT2) lineage commitment.
source: Inhibition of EHMT2 induces transcriptional, morphologic, and molecular changes consistent with alveolar type 2 (AT2) lineage commitment.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing increased AT2 markers and morphological features upon EHMT2 inhibition

claim: EHMT2 activity functions to support regenerative properties of KrasG12D tumors and normal AT2 cells.
source: Mechanistically, EHMT2 activity functions to support regenerative properties of KrasG12D tumors and normal AT2 cells—the predominant cell of origin of this cancer.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing impaired regenerative capacity upon EHMT2 inhibition/deletion

claim: EHMT2 inhibition prevents KrasG12D lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tumor formation and propagation and disrupts normal AT2 cell differentiation.
source: Consequently, EHMT2 inhibition prevents KrasG12D lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tumor formation and propagation and disrupts normal AT2 cell differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing reduced tumor formation and impaired AT2 differentiation upon EHMT2 inhibition

claim: Low gene EHMT2 expression in human LUAD correlates with enhanced AT2 gene expression and improved prognosis.
source: Consistent with these findings, low gene EHMT2 expression in human LUAD correlates with enhanced AT2 gene expression and improved prognosis.
evidence: Inferred from correlation analysis of TCGA data showing negative correlation between EHMT2 and AT2 gene signature

claim: EHMT2 is a critical regulator of Wnt signaling.
source: These data reveal EHMT2 as a critical regulator of Wnt signaling, implicating Ehmt2 as a potential target in lung cancer and other AT2-mediated lung pathologies.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing EHMT2 regulates Wnt signaling through RUVBL2-β-catenin interaction

claim: Ehmt2 is a potential target in lung cancer and other AT2-mediated lung pathologies.
source: These data reveal EHMT2 as a critical regulator of Wnt signaling, implicating Ehmt2 as a potential target in lung cancer and other AT2-mediated lung pathologies.
evidence: Speculative statement based on the findings that EHMT2 regulates Wnt signaling and cell fate in lung cancer and AT2 cells

claim: EHMT2 inhibition reveals an alternative cell-intrinsic mechanism of governing Wnt signaling in stem-like cells.
source: By discovering this alternative cell-intrinsic mechanism of governing Wnt signaling in stem-like cells, we are able to manipulate cell fate decisions to predictably limit the functionality of these cells to disable tumor propagation.
evidence: Inferred from the discovery that EHMT2 regulates Wnt signaling through a non-histone substrate mechanism

claim: EHMT2 activity functions to support regenerative properties of KrasG12D tumors and normal AT2 cells—the predominant cell of origin of this cancer.
source: In the context of lung, EHMT2 activity functions to support regenerative properties of KrasG12D tumors and normal AT2 cells – the predominant cell of origin of this cancer.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing EHMT2 is required for regenerative capacity in both tumor and normal AT2 cells

claim: The ability of AT2 stem populations to give rise to differentiated AT2 and AT1 cells is a critical feature that aids in maintaining the integrity of the distal alveolar compartment.
source: The ability of AT2 stem populations to give rise to differentiated AT2 and AT1 cells is a critical feature that aids in maintaining the integrity of the distal alveolar compartment (Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: Draws from established knowledge and citations to Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018

claim: Dysregulation of stemness is an underlying contributor to diseases of the airway, including idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and cancer.
source: How stemness is regulated and maintained is of considerable interest since its dysregulation is an underlying contributor to diseases of the airway, including idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and cancer.
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about stem cell dysregulation in lung diseases

claim: Wnt signaling is a master regulator of AT2 cell fate within the lung, paramount for development, homeostasis and damage repair.
source: Wnt signaling is a master regulator of AT2 cell fate within the lung, paramount for development, homeostasis and damage repair.
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about Wnt signaling in lung biology

claim: β-catenin loss in AT2 cells enhances AT1 conversion, indicating Wnt signaling functionally prevents differentiation of alveolar AT2 stem cells.
source: For example, β-catenin loss in AT2 cells enhances AT1 conversion, indicating Wnt signaling functionally prevents differentiation of alveolar AT2 stem cells (Frank et al., 2016; Nabhan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Frank et al., 2016; Nabhan et al., 2018

claim: Functional perturbation of EHMT2 activity enhances Wnt signaling, indicating impairment of AT2 plasticity, as well as the regenerative capacity of TPCs.
source: Our findings are consistent with this paradigm as functional perturbation of EHMT2 activity enhances Wnt signaling, indicating impairment of AT2 plasticity, as well as the regenerative capacity of TPCs.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental observations showing EHMT2 inhibition increases Wnt signaling and impairs regenerative capacity

claim: DKK1 is not expressed in AT2 cells.
source: Of note, DKK1 is not expressed in AT2 cells (Habermann et al., 2020), thus represents a distinct mechanism of Wnt regulation from what our work describes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Habermann et al., 2020

claim: Distinct niches provide exogenous Wnt ligands to support neighboring stem cells in the distal lung.
source: Recent reports (Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018; Zepp et al., 2017) describe, how Wnt regulation is remarkably nuanced within the distal lung with the discovery and characterization of distinct niches that provide exogenous Wnt ligands to support neighboring stem cells.
evidence: Supported by citations to Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018; Zepp et al., 2017

claim: Autocrine Wnt secretion has been proposed as a mechanism to self-sustain the Wnt signaling requirements while outside of the niche.
source: Although autocrine Wnt secretion has been proposed as a mechanism to self-sustain the Wnt signaling requirements while outside of the niche, our discovery provides a means to enable cell intrinsic regulation of β-catenin transcription, providing a safe switch to maintain AT2 cell identity when a mesenchymal Wnt-providing niche, is no longer tethered to the epithelial cell.
evidence: Draws from established knowledge about autocrine Wnt signaling

claim: EHMT2 loss at the time of tumor initiation leads to a significant reduction in tumor formation, as well as, tumor burden resulting in significantly increased overall survival.
source: In lung tumorigenesis, we observe that EHMT2 loss at the time of tumor initiation leads to a significant reduction in tumor formation, as well as, tumor burden resulting in significantly increased overall survival.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations in KPE and KE mice showing reduced tumor formation and increased survival

claim: Genetic cooperativity between Ras and Wnt signaling pathways has been reported and linked to cell fate effects.
source: Of note, genetic cooperativity between Ras and Wnt signaling pathways has been reported (Juan et al., 2014; Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011) and linked to cell fate effects.
evidence: Supported by citations to Juan et al., 2014; Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011

claim: Mutant beta catenin expression within Scgb1A1+ cells leads to a distal cell fate change and enhanced tumor formation.
source: In the context of Kras-mutant lung tumor initiation, genetic activation of Wnt signaling using mutant beta catenin within Scgb1A1 + cells leads to a distal cell fate change consistent with our results. However, in contrast to our AT2-derived tumor-initiation model, mutant beta catenin expression results in enhanced tumor formation within Scgb1A1+expressing cells (Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011

claim: Wnt signaling is necessary to maintain tumors.
source: Others have reported the necessity of Wnt signaling to maintain tumors (Juan et al., 2014) and suggested that Wnt gradients might be critical for self-renewal, in line with the necessity for a specific Wnt threshold to support this process (Tammela et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Juan et al., 2014 and Tammela et al., 2017

claim: Wnt gradients might be critical for self-renewal, in line with the necessity for a specific Wnt threshold to support this process.
source: Others have reported the necessity of Wnt signaling to maintain tumors (Juan et al., 2014) and suggested that Wnt gradients might be critical for self-renewal, in line with the necessity for a specific Wnt threshold to support this process (Tammela et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tammela et al., 2017

claim: EHMT2 activity functions similarly in primary AT2, as well as, Kras-transformed tumor cells, suggesting that TPCs may share functional features of their respective cell of origin.
source: EHMT2 activity functions similarly in primary AT2, as well as, Kras-transformed tumor cells, suggesting that TPCs may share functional features of their respective cell of origin.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations showing similar EHMT2-mediated regulation in both AT2 cells and TPCs

claim: The discovery that EHMT2 functions to directly regulate Wnt signaling deepens our mechanistic understanding of EHMT2 activity and presents potential opportunities for targeting in both lung cancer, as well as other AT2-mediated lung pathologies.
source: The discovery that EHMT2 functions to directly regulate Wnt signaling deepens our mechanistic understanding of EHMT2 activity and presents potential opportunities for targeting in both lung cancer, as well as other AT2-mediated lung pathologies.
evidence: Speculative statement based on the findings about EHMT2's role in regulating Wnt signaling
